els.text:
One HTML file.
A JSON model.
The renderer is the editor.
Agent-generated, brand-true, real-time editable presentations and assets — one portable HTML file, no office suite.
Drag anything · double-click to retype · ⌘Z undoes · → next slide · Esc contact sheet · F present · ⤓ PDF
Every slide is rows in a JSON array.

A row is {x, y, w, role, text}. Optional props turn the same row into a box, tile, bar, line, donut, svg or image. Nothing is implicit: the element adds no padding, radius or wrapping of its own — the role carries the type, the props carry the chrome.
Geometry is in model pixels on a fixed canvas (960×540 here). The editor scales the canvas to the window; print scales it to the page. Nothing reflows, so what you verify is what everyone sees.
Check a model without a browser:  node bin/validate.mjs model.json
Seven roles. One font and size per role.

A row never sets font, size, leading or tracking — the validator rejects it. Rows may carry weight, color, case and italics; inline runs carry bold, italic, underline, strike and color. Retheme by editing the roles; every deck follows.
Geometry lives in the layout. Content lives in the slide.
This slide's supertitle and title are bound to slots — {slot:'title', text:'…'} with no x, y or w on the row. The layout named 'content' owns that geometry for every slide that uses it.
Move a slotted row and the slide keeps a local override. The toolbar's “Apply to layout” promotes that geometry to the slot — every sibling slide follows.
Deck-scope slots (deck.slots) sit under every layout — for chrome shared by all layouts, such as a supertitle.
Chrome is drawn once, under every slide.
The rule and the footer at the bottom of this slide are master rows. The page counter renders inline inside the footer — same font, baseline and edge — never a hardcoded pin.

Edit a master row on one slide and the engine forks a slide-local override (override:'foot'). “Apply to all slides” pushes it back into the master. Delete it on one slide and only that slide hides it (hide:['foot']).
Drag a row. ⌘-click to multi-select and drag together.
Double-click to retype. Select a run and hit B, I, U or S.
The corner nib resizes width — and height when the row has one.
⌘Z undoes. The history survives a reload.
Floating toolbar: role segment · marks · the deck's own colors. No font pickers — roles are the type system.
The + menu adds Text (born Body, or bound to a free slot), Box and Slide.
Edits persist locally, per deck. ⤓ PDF prints what you see.
Every edit mutates the same model you authored. Read it back from the DECK object between the /*DECK*/ markers in the file.
bar:1 with h and bg · line:[x2,y2] · donut:72 · tile:1 — each is one row, draggable like any other. No SVG layer: a line is one rotated div, a donut one conic gradient.

⊞ or Esc opens the contact sheet: live thumbnails, three across. Click, ⌘-click and shift-click select; double-click opens; drag reorders; ⌫ deletes (never the last slide); ⌘C ⌘V ⌘D ⌘Z work as expected.

⤓ prints one page per slide at true model size, each painted with its own background. Safari ignores pixel page sizes, so the page is named Letter (A4 for document-a4) and the slide is zoomed to the printable width.
F or ⛶ enters fullscreen presentation: chrome hides, the backdrop takes the current slide's background, and the HUD peeks back while the pointer rests at the bottom of the screen.
node bin/create.mjs --model model.json --style style.json --out deck.html --format slides

SKILL.md is the authoring contract: inputs (content, format, style), the process, the model and style contracts, anti-patterns and three worked examples. Layout-parity verification is mandatory; the AE pixel diff runs whenever reference shots exist.

Formats: slides (16:9) is fully supported. carousel (1:1, 4:5) and document (Letter, A4) are page-size presets of the same model space — experimental: sizing, editing and PDF work; text does not flow across pages.
